content.comment_body: I'm having trouble connecting my [product_name] to my PC. My setup includes the [product_name] module and the [product_name] operator device. The Ethernet cable runs from the module to the operator device, which is then connected to my router. In the network view, the module displays a check mark, but not the operator device. All IP addresses are set within the 192.168.0.xx range, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, and gateway 192.168.0.1. The module shows as accessible when refreshed, but when I try to download a program or run a test, I receive an 'unable to access the remote device' error. Any suggestions would be appreciated. Cheers.

Could you specify the IP addresses and subnet masks assigned to each device in your setup? Please include the router, PC or laptop, and operator device. Also, is your PC set with a static IP or configured via the router?

I manually set the PC’s network configuration as advised elsewhere: PC: 192.168.0.30, 255.255.255.0, 192.168.0.1 [product_name] module: 192.168.0.60, 255.255.255.0, 192.168.0.1 [product_name] operator device: 192.168.0.62, 255.255.255.0, 192.168.0.1 Do I need to set anything else on the module to facilitate communication with the PC?
It appears you have a module without a display. How did you change its IP address, given the default is 192.168.0.1?
I changed the IP address via the operator device.
Have you selected the correct hardware type ([article_no]) in your settings? You can check this under File > Properties > Offline Settings > Hardware type.
[article_no] is selected in the network project window. When I try File/Properties, nothing appears, and right-clicking the module in network view shows the same [article_no].
I did not realize you were working in network mode. The option I mentioned applies only to diagram mode. If possible, upload your project as a ZIP file so we can take a closer look.
I've uploaded the project file as requested.

Everything in your project appears correct. I've attached a video demonstrating how to display modules successfully. If you follow the steps shown, your module should be visible. Please share a screenshot afterward.
My PC connects to the router via Wi-Fi; could this impact device connectivity?

Something seems off—the module’s IP address shows, but its MAC address and 'Yes' status are missing. Try connecting the module directly to the PC without the router to see if you can establish a connection.
I removed the MAC address for privacy; normally it does show 'Yes'.
Next time, please obscure details like the MAC address for clarity. Still, try connecting without the router as a troubleshooting step.
The issue is resolved—I installed an older Ethernet card and connected the PC to the router via cable instead of Wi-Fi. Thanks for your assistance.
Generally, using Wi-Fi shouldn’t affect the connection.
A related question from another user about connecting to the [company_name] [product_name] ([article_no]) was moved to a separate thread. Best regards, CS Moderator
I had the same issue—chose the wrong connection and network card for my [product_name] module. Be sure to avoid my mistake.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering difficulties achieving stable PC-to-[product_name] module connectivity even when network wiring and settings seem correct. There is uncertainty about configuring the right hardware type and mode within the software, and some discrepancies between accessibility indicators and actual device connectivity. Switching to a wired network connection helped resolve one user's issue.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable Ethernet communication and a straightforward process for downloading and testing programs on their [product_name] modules directly from their PCs, using current network setups and software interfaces.
